scope: any topic distinguishing an acute or recently-decompensated population from a chronic one
retrospective: WRITTEN AFTER THE TRIALS WERE KNOWN. This is a retrospective criterion like every other in this corpus. It is defensible on its logic; presenting it as prespecified would not be. Say so wherever it is applied.
primary_criterion: A trial belongs to the CHRONIC population if recent decompensation is NOT AN ENTRY REQUIREMENT. The distinction is not what proportion happened to be recently hospitalised -- it is whether a qualifying acute event was REQUIRED to enter.
why_design_not_percentage: A proportion is an accident of recruitment and varies between trials testing the same question. An entry criterion is a property of the trial and is checkable from the registration and protocol. A percentage threshold would also have to be defended as a number, and there is nothing to defend one with.
secondary_safeguard: For trials that PERMIT but do not REQUIRE recent decompensation: include when >= 80% meet the chronic definition, OR when the chronic subgroup's estimate is separately extractable, in which case use the subgroup. Below 80% with no extractable subgroup the trial is excluded and the reason recorded as COMPOSITION, not DESIGN.
mandatory_disclosure: Report the permitted proportion for EVERY included trial, in the review and not only in the object. A reader should see the mixture rather than infer homogeneity.

worked_cases.reason: a recent worsening-heart-failure event is its entry criterion, so it enrolled a decompensated population by construction. Excluded regardless of percentages.
worked_cases.already_matched: this object already excludes it on POPULATION with design-based reasoning; the rule confirms the existing call rather than changing it

worked_cases.reason: it enrolled chronic heart failure and PERMITTED randomisation during or shortly after admission. The 654 (10.4%) are a permitted minority, not the population.
worked_cases.disclosure_required: 10.4% permitted, to appear in the review

changes_to_included_sets: none on this topic. Where applying it changes an included set elsewhere, that is a FINDING and is reported, never a silent correction.
